prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its biologically active form, which made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After reading the full first-round exchange I keep B041 as a single prize part with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. All six of us agree on the science: the chain from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect in humans, through identification of the insulinotropic GLP-1(7-36) peptide, to drugs with benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, confirmed in independent randomized trials. It is original, mechanistically complete and mature, so recognition is timely. The three-way split on the third name is the only live question. I judge that a prize for physiology or medicine is best anchored in what was discovered about the hormone, with the drug class as its demonstrated consequence, and that is the strand the citation names. I do not need a second prize part, because B041 can carry three names alone and nobody has argued for splitting it.
statement.case_against: The weakest point of my configuration is credit. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide form is disputed with the Habener group, who are not on the supplied list, and the supplied record does not let us adjudicate it. If that dispute cannot be resolved, a citation resting on it is exposed, and the citation would then have to be worded around Mojsov's peptide chemistry and characterization, not first discovery of the hormone. Leaving out Knudsen can also be read as under-valuing the step that put the therapy into patients. Svenningsson and Perlmann make this case with real force, and I cannot say it is wrong, only that I think it answers a different question, which is whether the prize is for the therapy or the discovery. I also hold this view with only moderate confidence, because it depends on a reading of Mojsov's role that I have not been able to check against primary sources.

responses.point: Svenningsson argues that the short half-life of native GLP-1 was the obstacle, that identification of the active form alone did not make a therapy, and that a third slot cannot rest on a contested priority claim; he also asks whether Sawyers belongs on equal footing with Lydon and Druker in B004.
responses.response: Your argument on half-life is correct as pharmacology, and it is the strongest reason to take the Knudsen configuration seriously. Where I still differ is that the half-life problem could only be posed once the active form was known, so identification is the step that made the problem definable and not one of several parallel ones. I accept your condition: if the committee cannot confirm from the primary literature that Mojsov's contribution was a characterization step in its own right, then Drucker, Holst and Knudsen is the more defensible trio and I would vote for it over a dispute that stalls B041. On B004, I would put Sawyers on equal footing. Druker carried the clinical proof, Lydon the compound, and Sawyers the resistance biology that defined how the drug is used long term. I would not rank any of them below the others. I accept that your point on prior recognition of kinase inhibition lowers B004's novelty relative to a new modality, which is why it stays an alternative and not my lead.

responses.point: El-Manira says Knudsen's acylation work was a creative solution, not routine development, so she should rank ahead of Mojsov, and asks why B004 is placed above B035 given CAR-T as a new therapeutic modality.
responses.response: I accept that acylation and half-life extension was inventive, and I withdraw any suggestion that it was routine. My answer on B004 versus B035 is that I weigh attribution and completeness of the credited list alongside conceptual novelty. B004 has a clean trio with no absent originator, whereas B035 omits Eshhar and the group disagrees on Rosenberg. To move B035 above B004 I would need the committee to accept a configuration without Eshhar as faithful to the chimeric receptor concept, or a persuasive case that June and Sadelain alone describe the achievement. After Sandberg's and Linnarsson's points I now lean closer to you that CAR-T is the larger conceptual step, so I would regard the two as close fallbacks and would not object to B035 leading if the credit issue is cleared.

responses.point: Sandberg says B004 is largely drug development, that the upstream Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discovery is not credited, and that the central figures are already recognized; she also says a Mojsov inclusion should rest on peptide chemistry and characterization, and be tested against the primary literature.
responses.response: On GLP-1 I agree and will adopt your wording discipline: Mojsov's inclusion rests on characterization of the active peptide, and the citation should say so and not claim first discovery of the hormone. That is why my citation uses the phrase biologically active form. On B004, the missing upstream discovery is a fair objection, but the prize has often honoured the translational step that proved a molecular mechanism was druggable, and the prior recognition is of related ideas, not of this therapy. I treat it as a real reduction in novelty, not a disqualification.

responses.point: Linnarsson holds the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio with only moderate confidence and names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen as the fallback if the Mojsov priority question cannot be resolved.
responses.response: We hold essentially the same position and for the same reasons, including the same fallback. I would add one working rule for the vote: if the committee cannot agree on Mojsov, the right response is to move to Knudsen, and not to drop B041 or add a second part to make room. That keeps the prize on the one candidate on which all six of us agree on the science.

uncertainties: Whether the primary literature supports Mojsov's contribution as an independent characterization of GLP-1(7-36) distinct from the Habener group's work; I have not been able to resolve this from the supplied record.
Whether Habener's absence from the credited list leaves the attribution too incomplete for a clean citation.
Whether the committee will treat the prize as one for the discovery or the therapy, since the two give different third names.
Whether B035 can stand as a fallback without Eshhar, and whether B004's cleaner credit outweighs its lower conceptual novelty.
Long-term safety and the newest cardiovascular, renal and neurological indications are still being defined and should not be written into the citation.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My field is autoimmunity and rheumatology, and I have no documented collaboration with any credited GLP-1, CAR-T or BCR-ABL name. I do not infer personal ties from shared institutions or topics. No change from round 1, and no recusal is needed.
